figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of BindCLIP. A frozen CLIP-ViT encodes the image and the candidate captions; a single token–patch–depth optimaltransport coupling P reads semantic, entity/role, and spatial evidence from one correspondence state; an antisymmetric pair score produces the preferred caption.

Fig. 2. Three examples from the official SugarCrepe split, one per phenomenon, where frozen global CLIP prefers the compositionally wrong caption (negative margin) and BindCLIP reverses it (positive margin). Columns: object swap, relation replacement, attribute swap. In the object- and attribute-swap columns the two captions contain identical content words and differ only in which word binds to which region.
